topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Hallmarks Framework
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer establishes the lecture's learning outcomes, connects the material to prior lectures, and introduces the hallmarks of cancer conceptual framework.

topics.label: Growth Signaling and Proliferation Control
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta, deregulate cellular proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Block of Cellular Differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells fail to terminally differentiate, using examples from hematopoiesis and colonic crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome the Hayflick limit and bypass p53-mediated senescence and cell cycle arrest to achieve replicative immortality.

topics.label: Altered Cancer Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis and metabolic enzyme mutations to support tumor growth.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the requirement, timing, and molecular regulation of angiogenesis in sustaining tumor growth.

topics.label: Cancer Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the multistep cascade of cancer metastasis, from local tissue invasion and circulatory dissemination to colonization and associated genetic signatures.

topics.label: Closing Remarks and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarizes the overarching themes of cancer hallmarks, references recent literature, and concludes the session.
